# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-12 (Extended v107)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Winter/Summer Year 3)**: (1) Paris—Café Musain near Panthéon (Friends of the A B C meeting); le Petit-Picpus convent district (Valjean, Cosette sanctuary); M. Gillenormand's residences; Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district—Marius's attic cabinet); village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière (M. Mabeuf's cottage); Luxembourg gardens; (2) English provincial harbor towns (Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Staveford, Ravenmere, Ostcombe, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Dunby, Dungate, Torton). **Environmental conditions (Winter/early Summer Year 3)**: wind off water with salt/tar smell; light goes early; smoke lies flat; frost silvered hedges; chalk sun on forge wall; dog barks at nothing then goes quiet; bell for vespers rings thinly; bees hum in lavender.

## Primary Locations
**PARIS - LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus; convent complex with garden, chapel, burial vault. **M. GILLENORMAND'S RESIDENCES**: Rue Férou; Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire in Marais. **CAFÉ MUSAIN**: Near Panthéon, Rue Saint-Michel; headquarters Friends of the A B C; back room with argand lamp, two windows, private stairway on Rue des Grès. **GORBEAU HOVEL**: 50-52, Salpêtrière district; Marius's attic cabinet rented for 30 francs annually. **M. MABEUF'S COTTAGE**: Village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière; thatched cottage rented for fifty crowns yearly; three rooms and garden enclosed by hedge with well. **LUXEMBOURG GARDENS**: Solitary walk skirting parapet of Pépinière, Rue de l'Ouest side—location of recurring bench encounter.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette
Valjean integrated into convent life as assistant gardener; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Spiritual transformation complete. Cosette became convent scholar; thinks herself his daughter; adores him. Fauchelevent remains sole ally aware of full presence. Nuns do not suspect.

## Javert's Pursuit
Attached to Paris police after Valjean's escape. Investigated child abduction memory; followed mysterious lodger to Gorbeau house. **Current status (Winter Year 3)**: Established sentinels, organized traps and ambuscades; sure convict could not be far off.

## Marius Pontmercy: Development Continued

**Identity and age**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old; three years since left grandfather M. Gillenormand.

**Paternal legacy**: Colonel's written instruction regarding Baron title and Waterloo sergeant Thénardier. Lost medallion of black shagreen during move; convinced grandfather burned it.

**Political transformation**: Converted from childhood royalism to Bonapartism and republicanism (Autumn Year 3). **Recent change (Winter Year 3)**: Political fevers dissipated through reverie; Revolution of 1830 assisted calming. No longer held firm opinions but sympathies. Belonged to party of humanity; chose people above nation, woman above people. Pity directed to woman. Preferred idea to deed, poet to hero; admired book Job more than event Marengo. When meditating on boulevards, catching glimpse of fathomless space, mystery, human seemed very pretty to him.

**Material condition (Winter Year 3)**: Occupied Gorbeau house cabinet for 30 francs annually. Daily food cost: 20 sous (365 francs yearly). Clothing: 100 francs. Linen and washing: 100 francs. Total sustenance: 450 francs. Had no fireplace. Wardrobe: Two complete black suits; three shirts total.

**Professional status (Winter Year 3)**: Admitted to law practice; drew about seven hundred francs yearly from work. Learned German and English; employed in publisher M. Magimel's establishment (drew up prospectuses, translated newspapers, annotated editions, compiled biographies). **Refused advancement (Winter Year 3)**: M. Magimel offered lodging, regular occupation, fifteen hundred francs yearly. Marius refused: would renounce liberty, become hired man of letters, lose dignity.

**Philosophy of leisure and dreams (Winter Year 3)**: After succeeding in earning living with approach to certainty, stopped—thinking it good to be poor, retrencing time from work to give to thought. Sometimes passed entire days in meditation. Dreams reveal true character more surely than thoughts; reveal soul's depth utterly spontaneously. Real character found in aspirations more than deliberate ideas. Each dreams of unknown and impossible according to his nature.

**Pleasures and observations (Winter Year 3)**: Took long walks alone on outer boulevards, Champs-de-Mars, least frequented alleys of Luxembourg. Often spent half a day gazing at market garden, beds of lettuce, chickens, horse turning water-wheel. Attended occasional evening parties at homes of father's old generals when invited; wore new coat but attended only on freezing cold days as could not afford carriage.

**Attitude toward women (Winter Year 3)**: At period of abject misery, observed young girls turned round when he passed; he fled or hid with death in his soul, thinking they stared at old clothes and laughed; fact was they stared because of his grace and dreamed of him. Did not flee two women: bearded old woman who swept chamber (caused Courfeyrac to joke about his servant's beard); and little girl he saw very often and never looked at.

**Quarrel with grandfather (Autumn Year 3)**: Violent quarrel three years ago; remained on same terms without attempting to approach each other—"Marius was the brass vase, while Father Gillenormand was the iron pot." Grandfather's concealed suffering locked within breast.

**Relationship with Friends of the A B C (Winter Year 3)**: Met Courfeyrac at Place Saint-Michel; became good friends. Courfeyrac introduced him to Café Musain. Did not enter decidedly into group presided over by Enjolras but remained good friends. One old friend: **M. Mabeuf**—inclined more to old man; owed to him revolution within him; indebted for having known and loved father.

**Courfeyrac's advice (Winter Year 3)**: Warned: "Do not aspire to be venerable. Don't read so many books, and look a little more at the lasses...By dint of fleeing and blushing, you will become brutalized."

## M. Mabeuf

**Character and occupation**: Ecclesiastic, botanist, editor, man of books and flowers.

**Servant—Mother Plutarque (Winter Year 3)**: Sort of innocent spinster. Her cat Sultan filled her heart sufficiently. Never proceeded further than cat. Glory consisted in white caps. Knew how to read.

**Relocation and new residence (Winter Year 3)**: Carried off _Flora_, copper-plates, herbariums, portfolios, books; established himself near Salpêtrière in thatched cottage village of Austerlitz. For fifty crowns yearly got three rooms and garden enclosed by hedge containing well. On night of entrance, perceiving Mother Plutarque had melancholy air, tapped her shoulder and said with smile: "We have the indigo!"

**Philosophical disposition (Winter Year 3)**: Brains absorbed in wisdom or folly slowly accessible to actual life. Results in passivity resembling philosophy. Always ends in awakening but tardy. Habits of mind had regular swing of pendulum. Once mounted on illusion, went very long time even after illusion disappeared.

**Recent pleasure (Winter Year 3)**: Mother Plutarque reading romance aloud ("Bouddha and the Dragon"). M. Mabeuf struck in with low voice about dragon; called it good book, most beautiful legend in existence.

## The Mysterious Couple at Luxembourg

**Initial observation (over one year prior to current point)**: Marius noticed in Luxembourg walks a man approximately sixty years old and very young girl seated side by side on same bench, Rue de l'Ouest side, nearly every day. Man appeared military officer retired from service (robust, weary aspect); had kindly but unapproachable air; never let glance linger on others' eyes. Wore blue trousers, blue frock coat, broad-brimmed hat always appearing new, black cravat, dazzlingly white quaker shirt of coarse linen, white hair. Grisette called him "very tidy widower."

**Girl's initial appearance**: Thirteen or fourteen years old, thin, almost homely, awkward, insignificant, with possible promise of handsome eyes. Eyes always raised with displeasing assurance. Dress both aged and childish—badly cut gown of black merino, like convent scholar dress. Appeared to be father and daughter.

**First six months (then interruption)**: Marius observed couple briefly then paid no attention. They appeared not to see him. Conversed with peaceful, indifferent air. Girl chattered incessantly and merrily. Old man talked little; at times fixed eyes on her overflowing with ineffable paternity. Habit interrupted for nearly six months without Marius knowing why.

**Reunion and transformation (precisely at current point, summer Year 3)**: Marius returned to Luxembourg on serene summer morning in joyous mood. At first thought girl was another daughter, sister of former. Upon second examination recognized her as same. **In six months little girl had become young maiden.** Nothing more frequent than this phenomenon—there is moment when girls blossom in twinkling of eye, become roses all at once.

**Changed appearance (summer Year 3)**: No longer school-girl with felt hat, merino gown, scholar's shoes, red hands. Taste had come to her with beauty; she was well-dressed person clad in rich and simple elegance. Wore dress of black damask, cape of same material, bonnet of white crape. White gloves displayed delicacy of hand toying with carved Chinese ivory parasol handle; silken shoe outlined smallness of foot. Whole toilette exhaled youthful and penetrating perfume.

**Marius's continued indifference (summer Year 3)**: When she raised eyelids second time Marius approached, eyes deep celestial blue but in veiled azure nothing but glance of child. She looked at him indifferently as at brat running beneath sycamores or marble vase casting shadow on bench. Marius continued promenade, thought about something else. Subsequently returned to Luxembourg as usual, found "father and daughter" there but paid no further attention. He thought no more about girl now beautiful than when homely. Passed very near bench where she sat, because such was his habit.

## Friends of the A B C (Revolutionary Organization)

**Context (Autumn Year 3)**: Revolutionary quiver vaguely current. Youth moulting; people undergoing transformation. Friends of the A B C existed at Paris.

**Identity and purpose**: Declared themselves Friends of the A B C—the _Abaissé_,—the debased (the people). Wished to elevate people. Not numerous; secret society in embryonic state.

**Meetings (Autumn/Winter Year 3)**: Convened back room Café Musain; argand lamp lighted. Nearly all haranguing at haphazard; tossed words, caught up in turn. Peaceable tumults.

**Members**: Enjolras (believer, sober), Combeferre, Jean Prouvaire, Feuilly, Courfeyrac, Bahorel, Lesgle/Laigle de Meaux, Joly, Grantaire. Most students, cordial with working classes.

## English Provincial Towns (Updated)

**Population movements**: Yera Haskick left Dunstead for Kelmere; Rinelle quit Kelford for Torton; Kadrek Brackick followed to Torton. **Births (Dunstead)**: Son Ferald Stenworth and daughter Isvie Stenworth born to Luwyn Brackick. **New birth (Ostcombe)**: Son Zavus Prydenridge born to Wenelle and Rovus Prydenridge.

**Activities and observations (Winter/Spring Year 3)**: Isric Thornmere mended torn sleeve by window, said little; asked Wenelle "Will it rain, do you think?"—she shrugged. Rozek Stenenridge told Luena Stenenridge "You look tired"; Luena did not deny it. Yera Haskick laughed at story nobody else found funny; told Gadan Corrley (who did not deny looking tired) that Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood. Vesmira Thornmere and Wenelle Lindmere talked of weather, harvest, lame horse. Taric Corrley complained of aching back, as usual (previously Taric agreed salt price scandal with Pelia Lindmere). Taric walked long way round to avoid muddy square. Kadan bought ribbon at stall then regretted it.

**Claims and rumors (prior)**: Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures forged (claim). Wenelle Lindmere drowned crossing estuary (rumor, no body seen). Granary fire set on purpose (rumor). Kadan Corrley burned letter from Yera Haskick revealing mill ledger rewritten.

**Observations**: Rorald Lindmere gave Gadan Corrley solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Ravenmere. Gadan Corrley counted coins twice, came up penny short. Kassa remarked "I heard river is up again"; Yera Haskick said it always was in spring.

## Current Events (Winter Year 3)

**Paris student assembly**: Students of schools of law and medicine summoned to assemble Place du Panthéon at midday to deliberate on artillery of National Guard—conflict between Minister of War and "citizen's militia" over cannon parked in courtyard of Louvre.

**M. Gillenormand's rage**: Read announcement in Royalist sheet; flew into rage; denounced students as "pack of brats," Republicans forming "one nose and one handkerchief" with galley-slaves. Invoked Republican perfidy examples. Called progress madness, humanity dream, revolution crime, republic monster.

**New scheming (Winter Year 3)**: Aunt Gillenormand plotted to have Lieutenant Théodule (nephew in lancer regiment) take Marius' place in household. Théodule entered clad in plain clothes as bourgeois, discreetly introduced. M. Gillenormand, indulging in painful dream before entrance, thought no more of his grandnephew after reading.
